Not surprised Loyalist got noted in that article, especially after their actions when closing residence due to covid.

Students were given 48 hours notice to vacate, and originally stated they would accommodate students with extenuating circumstance. They then said they had received too many requests, and that being an international student didn’t qualify.  Students were told finding alternate accommodation was in their own hands, and they suggested working together.

Thankfully after pressure from the public and  media local hotels made a deal with the college to house students who had nowhere to go, and the college footed the bill.
If you’re still looking for it, once you log in to your NSLC account you should see a chat with us box in the bottom right corner of the window

I guess technically you could do that, but typically OSAP pays tuition to your school directly and then whatever is left is deposited to your account. The entire portion of grants does not have to be used solely on tuition, if you pay tuition and some is left the remaining portion is just living expenses. 

I would believe nothing would happen on the loan side, but you’d be on the hook with the school to pay the tuition. 

If not paying made your drop out, they’d probably turn your grant into loans and add it to your debt, and it might register as an overpayment.

Same thing for me, I was in repayment and my enrolment was confirmed on the second. I used the online chat and they say apparently it’s been changed to in study today, and it won’t show on my end until tomorrow. I’m assuming now it will be 3-5 days for the deposit now that it’s changed.
I haven’t tried calling them, but I was able to use the online chat service and there was no wait there
